class-cost-as-number.json.why: USD amounts are exact-decimal strings even when whole; the JSON number 20 is rejected so no consumer reads money as a number.

class-cost-not-tokens-times-rate.json.why: Each class cost is exactly tokens x rate / 10^6 (6.4); a fixture that disagrees would certify a wrong oracle.

priced-with-unpriced-dimensions.json.why: A case is either priced or unpriced; a priced expectation carrying unpriced_dimensions is contradictory.

total-nanodollars-float.json.why: Nano-dollars are an integer; 209000000.0 is a JSON float and money is never a float (6.4).

total-nanodollars-string.json.why: total_nanodollars is a 64-bit integer, not a string, so ledgers compare it without parsing text.

unpriced-without-dimensions.json.why: An unpriced expectation must name the uncovered dimensions so the test proves why the attempt is unpriced (M5, B3).

used-class-left-unpriced.json.why: Every token class the usage incurs is priced; leaving one out would price it at zero (6.3).
